lesson.title: First Volley: Use the Opening
lesson.hook: Two connected choices. Watch what your first shot creates.
lesson.liveIntro: Your approach moves them wide. This backhand volley is above the net, with the opposite side open.

th1A.name: What has the first volley actually earned?
th1A.sit: Their pass comes wider to your forehand. Recover into the next volley.
th1A.q: What has the first volley actually earned?
opts: Place the next volley with controlled depth

lines.A: You adjust and keep a generous target for the wider ball.
lines.B: This angle lands, but the wider contact leaves less room to force it.

th1A.take: A higher volley offers options. Read the next pass before choosing again.
th1A.payoff: A higher volley offers options. Read the next pass before choosing again.
th1A.principle: Use the height and space. Place it, then stay ready.
th1A.why: Compared with the low first volley, this ball arrives above the net and the opponent is displaced. A compact forward action can use the open side. Do not assume a winner: recover and split for the return they actually produce.

th1B.name: What has the first volley actually earned?
th1B.sit: Their stretched reply comes higher through the middle. Stay organised for the forehand volley.
th1B.q: What has the first volley actually earned?
opts: Place the next volley with controlled depth

lines.A: A sound controlled placement. The higher contact also offered the shorter angle.
lines.B: You use the higher contact and open side. Stay ready until the point is over.

th1B.why: Compared with the low first volley, this ball arrives above the net and the opponent is displaced. A compact forward action can use the open side. Do not assume a winner: recover and split for the return they actually produce.

th1.name: What does the higher contact offer?
th1.sit: Your approach moves them wide. This backhand volley is above the net, with the opposite side open.
th1.q: What does the higher contact offer?
opts: Place the volley back through the middle
Place the volley into the open side

lines.A: You send it toward their side. They get a more comfortable passing attempt.
lines.B: You use the height and space. They still get a racket to your compact volley.

summaries.10: The first choice fitted. The next ball needed a fresh decision.
summaries.11: Both choices fitted the contact and court you had. Keep reading as the point changes.
summaries.01: You adapted on the second ball. Compare what the first choice cost.
summaries.00: Compare the first choice, then read the next contact again. A landing alone does not prove a sound decision.

pro.label: Annacone · Now comes the easy part
pro.moment: Annacone’s volley lesson builds towards the satisfying finish: a short ball, a strong approach, then a volley the player can knock away. The approach has already done much of the work. The volley is the reward for creating that opening.
pro.read: Your next point: here the volley is above the net and the opponent is displaced. Use the opening, then prepare for the next reply.

drill.name: Two-ball read
drill.how: Have a partner feed one low volley and one above the net, while changing sides. Call “build” or “place” from the contact and court, then play a second volley.
